procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment of the Division Bench of the High Court dated September 13, 1985, which modified the Single Judge's order by setting aside the reinstatement of the respondent and permitting the Disciplinary Authority to proceed with disciplinary proceedings from the stage of giving a fresh show cause notice.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings:
1. Respondent filed a Writ Petition before a Single Judge.
2. Single Judge quashed the dismissal order and directed reinstatement, finding no evidence to support the charges and that the respondent was not given an opportunity to show cause against the punishment or provided a copy of the Inquiry Officer's report.
3. Appellants (Department) appealed to a Division Bench.
4. Division Bench agreed that the respondent was deprived of an opportunity to show cause against the punishment.
5. Division Bench modified the Single Judge's order by setting aside the reinstatement and allowing the Disciplinary Authority to proceed from the stage of issuing a fresh show cause notice.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture:
1. Appellants filed a Special Leave Petition in the Supreme Court.
2. The Supreme Court heard the petition after notice to the respondent.
3. The Supreme Court granted leave to appeal.
4. The Supreme Court noted that the Division Bench did not consider the Single Judge's judgment on merits.
5. The Supreme Court set aside the Division Bench's judgment and remanded the case to the Division Bench to dispose of the appeal on merits after hearing both parties.

decision.sentence_status: The penalty of compulsory retirement of the respondent from service is upheld.
directions: Set aside the judgment of the Division Bench of the High Court.

issue.issue_text: Whether it is necessary to give a second show cause notice against the punishment before the same was imposed on the respondent and to furnish him with a copy of the report of the Inquiry Officer in view of the amendment of clause (2) of Article 311 of the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Forty-Second Amendment) Act, 1976 and the consequential change brought about in Rule 15(4) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965.

facts: A government servant (the respondent) was found guilty of misconduct in a disciplinary inquiry.
The Disciplinary Authority dismissed him from service without giving him a second show-cause notice regarding the proposed punishment.
The High Court, at both the Single Judge and Division Bench levels, ruled that the dismissal was invalid because the respondent was not given this second opportunity to argue against the penalty.
law: The Constitution (Forty-Second Amendment) Act, 1976, amended Article 311(2) of the Constitution of India.
This amendment specifically deleted the requirement to provide a government servant with a "reasonable opportunity of making representation on the proposed penalty."
The amended proviso to Article 311(2) now expressly states that it is not necessary to give any opportunity to make a representation on the proposed penalty.

Consequently, Rule 15(4) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, was also amended to remove the provision for a second show-cause notice regarding the punishment.
application: The Supreme Court found that the High Court had completely overlooked the significant legal changes brought about by the Forty-Second Amendment.
The Court clarified that the only right to make a representation on a proposed penalty existed in Article 311(2) *before* the amendment.

Since that right was explicitly removed by the constitutional amendment, there is no longer any provision in law under which a government servant can claim a second opportunity to show cause against the punishment.

The Court noted that the constitutional requirement is now satisfied by holding a single inquiry where the employee is informed of the charges and given a reasonable opportunity to be heard on those charges, which was done in this case.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court rejected the respondent's claim, holding that due to the Forty-Second Amendment to Article 311(2) of the Constitution and the corresponding change in Rule 15(4), it is no longer necessary to provide a government servant with a second show-cause notice or an opportunity to make a representation against the proposed penalty before it is imposed.

arguments.issue_text: Whether it is necessary to give a second show cause notice against the punishment before the same was imposed on the respondent and to furnish him with a copy of the report of the Inquiry Officer in view of the amendment of clause (2) of Article 311 of the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Forty-Second Amendment) Act, 1976 and the consequential change brought about in Rule 15(4) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965.
appellant_arguments: The appellants implicitly argued that after the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution, it was no longer necessary to provide a second show cause notice against the proposed punishment or to furnish a copy of the inquiry report before imposing the penalty. Their appeal was against the High Court's decision which held the dismissal to be vitiated on this very ground.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that the order of dismissal was vitiated because he was not given an opportunity to show cause against the punishment before it was imposed and was not supplied with a copy of the Inquiry Officer's report.

statutes.act_name: Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965

cases.case_name: Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel
cases.principle: The right to make a representation on a proposed penalty, which was previously available under Article 311(2) of the Constitution, was removed by the Constitution (Forty-Second Amendment) Act. Therefore, there is no provision of law under which a Government servant can claim this right (a second opportunity to show cause against the punishment).

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A disciplinary authority may impose a penalty based on its findings on any or all of the articles of charge, provided those findings are supported by the evidence adduced during the inquiry.
obiter: When a Division Bench fails to consider the judgment of a Single Judge on its merits, the appropriate course is to remand the case back to the Division Bench for a decision on the merits after giving the parties an opportunity of being heard.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The respondent cannot claim a second opportunity to show cause against the punishment either under Article 311(2) of the Constitution or under Rule 15(4) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965. Consequently, the lower courts were not justified in holding that the order of dismissal was vitiated because the respondent was not given a second opportunity to make a representation against the punishment before it was imposed on him.
legal_tests_applied: Interpretation of Article 311(2) of the Constitution of India as amended by the Constitution (Forty-Second Amendment) Act, 1976.
Interpretation of Rule 15(4) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, as amended in consequence of the constitutional amendment.
Application of the precedent set in Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel, [1985] 3 S.C.C. 389.
